messages:

Cc: Arielle Soto <arielle@safeledger.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call — inference fit and spend guardrails

Jonas / team,

Thanks for the call earlier — quick notes from our side while they're fresh:
- Primary use: real-time fraud scoring for card-not-present transactions (pre-authorization).
- Traffic profile: ~2B tokens/month projected in steady state; peak windows during batch settlement at 1.5x baseline.
- Latency requirement: P95 target ~150ms; occasional tolerance to 300ms if downstream queuing is enabled.
- Current constraint: procurement is comfortable with a ~25k USD/month ceiling for a pilot proof-of-value; any ask above that will need finance sign-off.
- Pain: our proof-of-concept on another vendor had big variance in latency with small batch sizes and cold KV cache behavior. That killed our SLA.

Open asks we need from Redwood to move forward with a pilot:
1) an estimated TCO for 2B tokens/mo with options (hosted / dedicated / quantized) so we can compare to our internal runbook;
2) suggested pilot sizing (duration, capacity) and what measurable wins we should expect (cost/RPM, latency P95);
3) security/compliance checklist and any documentation required for procurement.

If you can get us a short one-page cost comparator and pilot asks by EOD tomorrow we can try to get budget pre-cleared for a 3-week pilot.

Thanks,
Michael Chen
Director, Payments Product
SafeLedger

--

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>

Subject: Budget gate playbook + pilot request — alignment on token levers and kickoff asks

Michael / Arielle — thanks again for the time today. Short recap and proposed next steps below (keeping this tight for procurement). I'm copying Marissa and Ben for pricing/ops detail.

TL;DR: We can run a scoped 3-week pilot aimed at validating latency SLOs and demonstrating 30–50% per-token cost reduction versus your current baseline through batching + prefix/KV caching + optional int8 quantized model. Preliminary estimate fits inside the $25k/month pilot ceiling if we scope to a limited traffic slice and use a dedicated small pool.

1) Confirmed pain points (from call)
- Latency spikes with small, unbatched bursts and cold KV cache events.
- Unpredictable unit cost at scale due to tokenization profile and long prompt prefixes.
- Procurement needs a clear, one-line TCO comparator and an operations checklist.

2) Proposed cost levers to realize savings
- Continuous batching: grouping requests where latency budget allows (expected effective token-cost reduction 1.7–3x depending on average request size).
- Prefix / KV caching: cache common conversation prefixes and prompt fragments; expect 10–25% token reduction on repeated workflows.
- Quantized model variant (int8): ~20–35% lower compute cost with small quality delta; can be used as fallback for non-critical traffic.
- Routing by policy: route non-latency-sensitive backfill to cheaper regions or quantized instances.

3) Quick TCO ranges (very high-level, for procurement gating) — assumptions: 2B tokens/mo baseline, mixed queries (avg payload 250 tokens), peak buffers included
- Hosted (managed): $X = ~$45k/mo (baseline) — highest manageability, higher unit cost.
- Dedicated (small pool + autoscale): $Y = ~$28k–35k/mo depending on commitment and batching effectiveness.
- Dedicated + quantized + caching: $Z = ~$15k–22k/mo achievable in aggressive batching/caching scenario (pilot target).
(We will produce an itemized one-page comparator PDF for procurement by tomorrow.)

4) Pilot proposal (recommended)
- Scope: 3 weeks, dedicated small GPU pool, 2 traffic slices (1% production-like traffic for latency SLOs; 5–10% shadowed traffic for cost measurement).
- Success criteria: P95 latency <= 200ms on the 1% slice; verified per-token cost reduction >= 30% vs your baseline; no functional regressions on scoring output.
- Deliverables: daily dashboards (latency, token counts, cost per 1k tokens), weekly review, final ROI write-up and SOW-ready TCO comparator.

5) Ops / procurement asks from SafeLedger (what we need from you)
- Procurement contact and confirmation that $25k/mo pilot ceiling is the target (or the maximum authorized).
- A short list of sample prompts / traffic extracts (you mentioned a CSV) for more accurate cost modeling.
- Security questionnaire contact — we can share our SOC2 docs and the minimal evidence pack.

Attachments: pilot-scope.pdf (pilot flow + instrumentation), prompt-samples.csv (we'll use these to model token splits).

Next steps / timeline
- Tomorrow (EOD): Marissa will share a one-page cost comparator + suggested pilot pricing.
- Monday: finalize SOW and get procurement contact; begin security questionnaire exchange.
- Target kickoff: within 7–10 business days after procurement sign-off.

If any of the assumptions above are off (budget, traffic, latency tolerance), flag and we'll re-scope.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0198

Michael — adding pricing detail for the pilot so procurement has a direct line item to review. I'm keeping the numbers conservative given gating constraints.

Pilot pricing proposal (3-week scope)
- Pilot flat fee: $12,000 (covers Dedicated pool, baseline monitoring, and up to 1M tokens/day ingestion for the scoped slice).
- Measurement credits: if we validate >30% per-token savings vs baseline, we apply a $4,000 credit toward first month of Dedicated usage.
- Optional extended telemetry / custom tracing: $2,500 add-on if you want deeper integration with your observability stack.

Notes:
- The pilot flat fee is intended to stay within procurement comfort at ~$25k/month equivalent (3-week fraction). If procurement needs a lower cap, we can shrink the traffic slice or shorten pilot duration.
- Attached: pricing-sheet.xlsx (line-item breakdown) and a one-page TCO comparator (pdf) — Jonas will attach the comparator to his follow-up.

Happy to hop on a 15-minute procurement intro call if helpful — I can bring legal/finance to answer SOW and billing questions.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
